items.heading: Instead of One Number, Use
items.text: Instead of one number, use The 4-Stage Education Budget Map to think about spending across your child's whole educational journey. Each stage has a different job to do, a different typical cost range, and a different risk if you underfund it.

items.heading: These Are Commonly Reported Ranges
items.text: These are commonly reported ranges from education-cost research and industry surveys, not fixed prices, your child's actual city, school choice, and stream will move these up or down. Use them to size your own plan, not as a target to match.

items.heading: Stage 1, Foundation Years (Preschool
items.text: Stage 1, Foundation years (preschool through primary school). The job here is building basic literacy, numeracy, and school habits. Costs are usually the most flexible stage-to-stage, since a wide range of good options exist at different price points, and switching schools later is disruptive but not catastrophic.

items.heading: Stage 2, Growth Years (Middle
items.text: Stage 2, Growth years (middle school through class 10). The job shifts to building subject depth and study habits, and this is usually where private tuition first appears alongside school fees. Costs step up moderately, and this is a good stage to build the habit of saving toward the next two, more expensive stages.

items.heading: Stage 3, Decision Years (Classes
items.text: Stage 3, Decision years (classes 11-12, entrance-exam preparation). The job is preparing for a specific stream, board result, or competitive entrance exam. This is typically one of the two most expensive single-year stages, especially if coaching is involved, and it is time-boxed, the spending window is short and cannot be delayed.

items.heading: Some Industry and Financial
items.text: Some industry and financial-planning surveys report urban, middle-income Indian families spending in the range of 20-30% of household income on education broadly across fees, tuition, and related costs.

items.heading: Among Households That Use Private
items.text: Among households that use private coaching specifically, that coaching cost alone has been reported at roughly 16.5% of household per-capita spending in national survey data.

items.heading: Hsbc's Global Value of Education
items.text: HSBC's global Value of Education research found a large share of parents fund education from day-to-day income, with many reporting they cut leisure spending, work longer hours, or reduce their own long-term savings to make it work, a sign that many families are stretching, not comfortably budgeting.
